judgments.rationale: The existing reading in C0002 fully and faithfully reflects the introductory scope of paragraph (2) and the specific requirement of subparagraph (B). It preserves the actor ('the employee'), mandatory modal force ('shall'), governing condition regarding foreseeable leave for planned medical treatment under subparagraph (C) or (D) of subsection (a)(1) or subsection (a)(3), the 30-day notice requirement, and the exception where treatment requires leave to begin in less than 30 days. No necessary substantive correction or governing qualification is omitted, so leaving the reading unchanged is supported.

source_spans.quote: (2) Duties of employee In any case in which the necessity for leave under subparagraph (C) or (D) of subsection (a)(1) or under subsection (a)(3) is foreseeable based on planned medical treatment, the employee—

(B) shall provide the employer with not less than 30 days’ notice, before the date the leave is to begin, of the employee’s intention to take leave under such subparagraph, except that if the date of the treatment requires leave to begin in less than 30 days, the employee shall provide such notice as is practicable.
